 JUDGMENT
Challenging the adequacy of the compensation granted under the impugned award, the claimant in LAC No.17/1999 on the file of the Prl. Senior Civil Judge, Mangalore, has preferred this appeal.
2. The appellant was the claimant and respondents in this appeal were the respondents before the Trial Court.
For the purpose of convenience, the parties are referred to henceforth according to their ranks before the Trial Court.

3. Brief facts leading to this appeal are that, the claimant's lands totally measuring 3.59 acres in Sy.Nos.83/1, 82/2A and 88-2A3 of Peramannur Village, Mangalore Taluk were acquired vide preliminary notification dated 27.07.1995.
The Land Acquisition Officer (hereinafter referred to as 'the LAO') passed an award on 08.06.1998 determining the market value of the acquired lands at Rs.9,000/- per cent.

The claimant sought reference under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act,
1894 (hereinafter referred to as 'the Act').
The Trial Court determined the market value at Rs.43,000/- per cent which was challenged by respondent No.1/LAO in MFA No.667/2012.
This Court set aside the said award and remanded the matter to the Reference Court to reconsider the same in accordance with law.
4. The respondents, after remand, objected the claim petition denying the prayer of the claimant to determine the market value at Rs.1,00,000/- per cent.
Respondent No.2 admitted that the lands are acquired for the purpose of construction of MESCOM building and adjacent to the acquired lands,
MESCOM
has its official quarters.
5. The claimant examined two witnesses as PW-1 and PW-2 and got marked Ex.P1 and Ex.P2.
However, PW-1 and PW-2 were not kept present for cross-examination.
Respondent No.2 examined one witness as RW-1 and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R9.

The Trial Court, on hearing the parties held that the acquired land is situated beyond the Corporation limits, outside the town limits, away from railway station, bus stand and harbour, determined the market value at Rs.15,000/- per cent by deducting Rs.1,000/- per cent towards the cost of development on the ground that there is hillock on one side of the acquired lands and
finally determined the market value at Rs.14,000/- per cent.
Being aggrieved, the claimant is in appeal seeking for enhanced compensation.
6. Sri.

Sandesh J.Chouta, learned Senior counsel appearing for Sri.Shakeer Abbas M., learned counsel for the claimant submits that the Trial Court has committed an error in determining the market value of the acquired lands at Rs.14,000/- per cent.

It is submitted that the Trial Court failed The Ullal Jumma Masjid And vs The Land Acquisition Officer And on 12 July, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/149671719/

It is further submitted that as per the Commissioner's report, the distance between the acquired lands and Thokkottu - Konaje bus route is 381/2 feet and the lands are within half a kilometre from Thokkottu junction.
Hence, the Trial Court ought to have determined the market value atleast at Rs.33,000/- per cent as per Ex.P1.

It is also submitted that the Trial Court failed to appreciate that around the acquired lands, there are buildings and the distance between the acquired lands and Mangalore University is 71/2 kms, Yenapoya Medical College is at 4 kms from the lands and P.A.Engineering College at 9 kms.

Hence, the Trial Court ought to have determined the market value of the subject lands atleast at Rs.33,000/- per cent keeping in mind the fact that the city bus route passes through the acquired lands.

In support of his contention, he placed reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of P.Ram Reddy and Others v. Land Acquisition officer, Hyderabad Urban Development Authority, Hyderabad and Others.1

Hence, he seeks to allow the appeal.
7.

Per contra, Sri.H.V.Devaraju, learned counsel appearing for the respondent No.2 and the learned Additional Government Advocate appearing for the respondent No.1, in chorus, support the impugned judgment and award of the Reference Court and submit that after remand, the claimant failed to tender PW-1 and PW-2 for cross- examination, hence, their evidence is required to be discarded.

It is submitted that RW-1 has produced a number of sale deeds at Ex.R2 to Ex.R7 and certified copy of the guidance value at Ex.R8 which clearly indicate that the market value of the acquired property is between Rs.6,000/- and Rs.9,000/- per cent and the LAO has rightly determined the market value at Rs.9,000/- per cent which does not call for any enhancement.
Hence, they seek for dismissal of the appeal.

Considering the submissions of both sides and on examining the materials on record, the point that arises for consideration is:
"Whether the impugned judgment and award calls for any interference"?
ANALYSIS 9.

It is not in dispute that the claimant's lands totally measuring 3.59 acres in Sy.Nos.83/1, 82/2A and 88-2A3 of Peramannur Village, Mangalore Taluk were acquired vide preliminary notification dated 27.07.1995.
The LAO determined the market value at Rs.9,000/- per cent and passed the award on 08.06.1998.
The claimant sought reference and the Trial Court re-determined the compensation at Rs.43,000/- per cent vide judgment and award dated 28.07.2011.
The respondents challenged the Trial Court judgment in MFA No.667/2012.
This Court set aside the judgment and award dated 28.07.2011 and remanded the matter back to the Trial Court to reconsider afresh in accordance with law.
10. Admittedly, after remand the claimant who had adduced evidence of PW-1 and PW-2, failed to offer them for cross- examination.
The respondent No.2 - beneficiary of the acquisition, examined The Ullal Jumma Masjid And vs The Land Acquisition Officer

and got marked Ex.R1 to Ex.R9 mainly the certified copies of the sale deeds of the relevant years to demonstrate the value of the acquired land.
The evidence of PW-1 and PW-2 cannot be looked into as they were not available for cross- examination after remand.
The Commissioner's report dated 16.10.2008 available on record indicates that the Commissioner was appointed on an application made by the claimant.
The respondents neither objected nor opposed the report of the Commissioner.
The report of the Commissioner indicates that the Commissioner visited the spot on 20.08.2008 in the presence of the officials of the respondents.
The Commissioner submitted the report mainly with regard to the distance of the acquired lands and its potentiality with other areas for the purpose of determination of compensation.

As per the report,
the location of the acquired properties is as follows:
i) Acquired property is within the distance of 381/2 feet from Thokkottu - Konaje bus route ii) The distance from Thokkottu junction to the acquired property is only half a kilometre away.
iii) The Commissioner noted the distance between the acquired property and the important places as under:
a) Mangalore University - 71/2 kms.
b) Yenapoya Medical College - 4 kms.
c) P.A.Engineering College - 9 kms.
iv) The Commissioner noted that the acquired property consists of buildings belonging to MESCOM and there is direct road access to the property in question from the main road on the southern side.
11.
The aforesaid report of the Commissioner is neither objected by the respondent nor has the Trial Court taken note of it while determining the market value.
The learned Senior counsel appearing for the claimant heavily placed reliance on Ex.P1, the admitted market value of the property to the converted land in the vicinity.
He refers to Sl.No.43 which pertains to Peramannur Village.
Ex. P1
indicates the four different kinds of market value based on the distance and accessibility.

The relevant portion of Ex.P1 is extracted hereinbelow:
Sl. Village Adjacent Adjacent Within 1 Beyond 1 No.
Name to Highway to city bus km from km from on both route on bus route bus route sides both sides 43 Peramannur 45,000 33,000 20,000 15,000 12
. As per the Commissioner's report, the distance between the acquired property and Thokkottu - Konaje bus route is 381/2 feet and it is half a kilometre away from Thokkottu junction.
The Commissioner's report indicates that there is direct road access to the property in question from the The Ullal Jumma Masjid And vs The Land Acquisition Officer And

4 main road towards the southern side which shows that the acquired property fall within 1 km from the bus route.
Therefore, as per Ex.P1, the market value of the acquired lands can be fairly assessed at Rs.20,000/- per cent.

13. Learned Senior counsel for the appellant placing reliance on the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of P.Ram Reddy and others referred to supra submits that the suitability of the acquired lands for putting up of building has to be taken into account for determination of compensation.
He submits that admittedly the respondent No.2 has constructed the quarters for its employees.
Hence, the determination of market value to the acquired lands should be higher than the Commissioner's report as well as Ex.P1.
The said submission is taken note of only for the purpose of rejection as the subject lands were acquired for putting up sub-station and quarters of MESCOM.

Merely because some structures have been put up on the acquired lands, that itself cannot be the basis to consider the entire area as a fully developed area as on the date of notification / acquisition.

This Court has already taken note of Ex.P1 and the Commissioner's report referred supra and determined the market value at Rs.20,000/- per cent considering the acquired lands have a potential for non-agricultural purposes.
Hence, contrary contentions urged by the appellant merit no consideration.

The Trial Court committed an error in assessing the market value of the acquired lands at Rs.14,000/- per cent after deducting the development cost which is contrary to the Commissioner's report as well as Ex.P1.
14.
The respondents have adduced the evidence of RW-1 in support of their case and placed reliance on Ex.R2 to Ex.R7, the sale deeds of different dates between 1994 and 1995.

Perusal of the evidence of RW-1 with reference to the exhibits referred supra indicates that the market value / sale consideration shown in the aforesaid exhibits ranges between Rs.7,000/- and Rs.9,000/- per cent.
Admittedly, in those sale deeds, the extent of lands were very small.
Hence, that cannot be taken as the basis to determine the market value of the subject lands.
In the instant case, the respondents have acquired the lands measuring 3.59 acres which is comparatively larger than the lands found in Ex.R2 to Ex.R7.
Hence, the evidence of RW-1 and exhibits cannot be the basis to determine the market value of the subject lands.

15. Though this Court in MFA No.667/2012 observed that in the earlier round of litigation the Trial Court was in error in relying on Ex.P1 alone, even after remand the respondents neither objected the Commissioner's report nor Ex.P1.

This clearly indicates that the acquired lands have potentiality to be used for non-agricultural purposes and are very near to Thokkottu - Konaje bus route and just half a kilometre away from Thokkottu junction.
In other words, the acquired lands are just half a kilometre away from the National Highway.
Hence, the contrary contentions urged by the respondents merit no consideration and are accordingly rejected.
16. The Trial Court committed error in determining the market value of the acquired lands at Rs.14,000/- per cent which is contrary to the evidence on record.

This Court, taking note of the Commissioner's report as well as Ex.P1 and after considering the oral testimony of RW-1 and exhibits produced by the respondents, is of the considered view that it would be just and appropriate to determine the market value of the acquired lands at Rs.20,000/- per cent with all statutory benefits and interest.
